examples.label: Ranked shortlist
examples.text: A short set ranked by benefit against effort, cost and obligations; not a directory. List strong candidates with one open blocker separately. Zero results is fine; never pad.

examples.label: Conference speaker calls
examples.text: {{SECTOR}} or related conferences in the next six months that take outside speakers (talk, workshop, demo, panel, poster). Online anywhere; in person only in {{HOME_REGION}}. English or another founder language, online slots 08:00 to 23:00 {{TIMEZONE}}, free to apply and present.

examples.label: Online demo slots, next 14 days
examples.text: Online {{SECTOR}} or startup meetups and demo nights in the next 14 days where outside founders can present, even for 2 to 5 minutes. English or another founder language, slots 08:00 to 23:00 {{TIMEZONE}}, free.

examples.label: Launch platforms and directories
examples.text: Active launch platforms and directories with a free, current submission route for products like {{STARTUP_NAME}}, with lasting discovery among its users.

examples.label: Communities and chat
examples.text: Active {{SECTOR}} communities, forums and chat spaces where {{STARTUP_NAME}} can be discussed or shown within the rules.

examples.label: Media and creators
examples.text: Newsletters, creators, podcasts and trade media covering {{SECTOR}}, with an editorial or contact route and an audience that fits {{STARTUP_NAME}}.

examples.label: General marketing sweep
examples.text: Any enabled MK category. Add or improve practical marketing work (channel, contact, community, content idea, asset, website or listing fix, recurring action); no application route needed. Use existing categories. Prefer free or cheap work, but keep strong ideas with a fair cost.

examples.label: Grants and public funding
examples.text: The whole scope, including non-government routes with real non-dilutive support. Prefer a material benefit with a realistic path for the stated applicant; rank lower anything needing an unconfirmed consortium, sponsor or invitation. Apply {{CONSTRAINTS}} as hard filters.

examples.label: Startup support programs
examples.text: Structured programs with a live or rolling intake and a defined support offer: pre-accelerators, accelerators, incubators, venture studios, residencies, fellowships, mentoring. A label is not enough; skip directories, investor applications, one-off events, and programs whose only benefit is money, credits or publicity. Rank by value against dilution, cost and founder time, using {{CONSTRAINTS}}.

examples.label: Open-source project support
examples.text: Only if the product or part of it is open source. Programs meant to support open-source projects or maintainers: funding, paid maintenance, security, documentation, governance, fiscal hosting, bounties, travel. The company qualifies only if the rules allow it and the benefit goes to the open-source work.

examples.label: Perks, credits and in-kind resources
examples.text: Material free or subsidized resources (cloud, compute, AI and API credits, software, data, security, legal, accounting, marketing tools, workspace, hardware) with an application or activation route the terms allow for this applicant and use. Keep open-source-only and commercial terms apart. Rank by usable benefit after limits, expiry, required spend and lock-in.

examples.label: Market access and customers
examples.text: Defined paths to users, buyers, testers or distributors: pilots, design-partner programs, sandboxes, marketplace or integration listings with real discovery, channel or co-sell access, vendor onboarding. The official source must describe the access after acceptance; exposure or "become a partner" is not enough. Say which offer each route serves. Prefer near-term feedback, pilots or revenue over prestige.

examples.label: Partnerships and ecosystem
examples.text: A named organization with a defined way to start a relationship: application, joining process, partner request, integration route, collaboration call, co-marketing proposal. Memberships only with concrete value. Name the counterparty, what each side gives and what follows acceptance; one target per route.

examples.label: Visibility and recognition
examples.text: Awards, rankings, hackathons, launch features, pitch or demo events and media programs with a live entry or judging process (conferences and meetups: EV1, EV2). Fixed dates within six months; rolling routes only if usable now. The outcome must be public (feature, award, shortlist, selected launch, public demo); recognition without money counts. Hackathons must accept {{STARTUP_NAME}} or a related entry.

examples.label: Platform startup programs
examples.text: Startup, partner, researcher or maintainer programs of AI, cloud, developer and app platforms relevant to {{SECTOR}}, with a route usable now and a defined outcome (credits, technical access, support, a grant, an integration or distribution benefit). Taxonomy labels are search coverage, not proof a program exists; a free tier or trial is not a program.

examples.label: Legal, IP and standards
examples.text: Routes whose main value is foundation support, standards work, governance, or practical IP, licensing or compliance help, with a concrete link to {{STARTUP_NAME}}. Real outcomes (admission, working-group seat, audit, licensing help, patent or trademark support) count; logos, member lists and open invitations do not.

examples.label: Angels and early-stage funds
examples.text: Active angels, syndicates, scouts, and pre-seed or seed funds investing at {{STARTUP_NAME}}'s stage, in {{SECTOR}}, in companies from {{COUNTRY}} or {{HOME_REGION}}, with a public way in (form, pitch submission, introduction path, office hours). Record stage, ticket size and focus only as published.

examples.label: Grants and prizes as money
examples.text: Non-dilutive money for the company or a founder: grant awards, foundation grants, prize money, tax credits or refunds, equity-free program cash, stipends. Track amount, currency, payment timing and conditions; if a PO program is the route, link it instead of adding a second target.

examples.label: Debt and alternative financing
examples.text: Loans and credit open to a {{ENTITY_TYPE}} in {{COUNTRY}} at this stage: term or startup loans, credit lines, guaranteed or public loans, microloans, venture debt, invoice or equipment financing, revenue-based financing, with published terms or a documented application route.

examples.label: Crowdfunding and community
examples.text: Equity, community share, rewards and pre-order platforms, and sponsorship or donation programs, that accept a {{ENTITY_TYPE}} from {{COUNTRY}} in {{SECTOR}} and have an audience that fits {{STARTUP_NAME}}.

examples.label: Weekly review
examples.text: No new search. Review this section's targets dated in the next 14 days, overdue, or still open: re-check each official page, update changed dates, rules or links, and set closed ones to the matching status. Add a target only for a directly related new round. End with what changed and what needs a decision.

examples.label: Research a topic
examples.text: Topic: [write it here before running]. Official and primary sources first, then reputable secondary ones. Add only targets that fit the scope and {{STARTUP_NAME}}.

examples.label: Program facts
examples.text: Record only what the official rules or application page support. Route: open, rolling, capped or invitation; next action; deadline with time zone; direct link. Applicant: the product, a founder personally, or the company; can it apply alone; required partners; never carry eligibility from one to another. Eligibility: stage, company age, revenue, headcount, sector, location, IP terms. Benefit: amount, currency, duration, expiry, timing. Costs: fees, equity, required spend, co-financing, exclusivity, IP or data terms, reporting, attendance, travel. Effort: documents, interviews, review time. Silence means unknown, never zero, free or eligible; drop candidates missing a material fact.

examples.label: Conference speaker calls
examples.text: A verified, open call for papers or presenter slot for outside speakers; attend-only does not count. Check the deadline, and that speakers need not buy a ticket or sponsor.

examples.label: Online demo slots
examples.text: A current, direct registration or application link for a speaking or demo slot open to outside founders. Record the date and time in {{TIMEZONE}}.

examples.label: Listings
examples.text: Official submission URL, active process, eligibility, cost, deadline, and no equivalent listing already tracked.

examples.label: Communities
examples.text: Active community, working entry URL, rules that allow the intended participation, a relevant channel. Record account-age, karma, approval or timing rules.

examples.label: Media and creators
examples.text: Official submission form or current contact route, audience fit, rules, deadline. Published contact details only; outlet still active.

examples.label: Grants, tenders, tax credits
examples.text: Also: eligible activities and stage (limits on software, research, commercial or open-source work, IP, publication); payment or reimbursement model, eligible costs, upfront cash, VAT or sales tax, caps on cumulative public aid (de minimis or similar). Tenders: supplier requirements, deliverables, payment terms; this is contract revenue. Tax credits: refundable or not, and what spending they need.

examples.label: Startup programs
examples.text: Also: length, format, schedule, founder time, attendance, travel or relocation, which founders take part; next cohort; investment terms; workload (deck, demo, references, interviews, documents); for founder-group programs, whether the person or the company applies. Note the best fit, main blocker and next step.

examples.label: Open-source support
examples.text: Also: open-source conditions (license, public repository, maintainer role, project age and activity, commercial use), eligible work and deliverables, matching funds, milestones, renewal.

examples.label: Credits, resources, platform programs
examples.text: Also: exact service, units, permitted use (open-source or commercial), duration, expiry, renewal, what happens after. Separate the headline maximum from the usable amount. Check card verification, minimum spend, overages, required integrations or referrals, telemetry, lock-in. Mark each as actionable now or conditional; never record zero or a guarantee because the terms are silent.

examples.label: Market access
examples.text: Also: which product or use case; direct access or via referral, invitation, partner or procurement registration; the concrete access after acceptance (pilot, customer interviews, test environment, approved listing, co-selling); pilot scope, paid or unpaid, success criteria; commissions, certification, security review, data handling. A logo, directory entry or contact form is not customer access.

examples.label: Partnerships
examples.text: Also: counterparty and exact route; what each side gives; revenue share, minimum spend, exclusivity, brand, technical and reporting duties; approval steps. Skip sources that only say "become a partner". Acceptance never guarantees an integration, endorsement, audience or revenue.

examples.label: Visibility and recognition
examples.text: Also: self-submission or who may nominate; the real public outcome versus a private review or badge; judging criteria, content rights, exclusivity, winner duties. Hackathons: existing projects allowed, new build or attendance required, who owns the result. Media: earned coverage, contributor piece, listing or paid placement; a contact form is not an editorial route.

examples.label: Legal, IP and standards
examples.text: Also: license compatibility, membership status, jurisdiction; the concrete outcome versus recognition; dues, time, voting duties, CLA or DCO terms, IP assignment, patent pledges, indemnity. For IP or compliance help: provider, scope, territory, what is actually protected. A license does not prove ownership and a founder may not bind the company; unresolved ownership or signing authority is a blocker.

examples.label: Investors
examples.text: On the investor's own site or filings: active (recent deals or a current fund), stage, sector and location focus, published ticket size, the way in. Published contact routes only. Never invent portfolio companies, people or check sizes.

examples.label: Lenders and funding platforms
examples.text: In the official terms: who can apply (company age, revenue, location, legal form), amounts, full cost (interest, fees, warrants, revenue share, commission), repayment or payout schedule, guarantees, collateral, covenants, campaign limits, decision time. Never estimate rates or amounts the source does not state.

examples.label: Review of existing targets
examples.text: Open each target's official link and compare it with the fields. Change only what the page now shows differently, add the check date to the note, and set closed or vanished ones to the matching status.

examples.label: Basics
examples.text: Closed, expired, past or not-yet-open items; waitlists or invitations with no usable path; duplicates under any name or URL; items known only from aggregators or news, without the organizer's page; anything with an unverifiable route, eligibility, benefit, cost or deadline.

examples.label: Conferences
examples.text: Events more than six months out; in-person outside {{HOME_REGION}}; attend-only events; pitch competitions (PO7); pay-to-speak or sponsor-only slots; no language the founders present in; online slots outside 08:00 to 23:00 {{TIMEZONE}}.

examples.label: Online demo slots
examples.text: In-person events, events beyond 14 days, slots outside 08:00 to 23:00 {{TIMEZONE}}, passive webinars, paid participation, no working registration link.

examples.label: Listings
examples.text: Dormant platforms, paid-only listings, ad marketplaces, platforms that forbid self-submission or products like {{STARTUP_NAME}}.

examples.label: Communities
examples.text: Inactive, closed or off-topic communities, and those that ban self-promotion. A cold link drop is not a contribution.

examples.label: Media
examples.text: Paid-placement-only outlets, generic PR agencies, unreachable contacts, poor audience fit, invented contact details.

examples.label: Grants
examples.text: Debt, equity, convertibles or revenue-based financing (FU); recognition-only awards; intermediary pages without a live official route; paid applications, membership or consultancy before applying. For staff, co-financing, travel or attendance rules, follow {{CONSTRAINTS}} instead of excluding outright.

examples.label: Startup programs
examples.text: Investor-only applications, pitch competitions, directories, webinars, one-off events and courses outside a structured program; entry fees, paid membership or consultancy; equity terms not published in full (an unstated term is never zero); programs whose only benefit is publicity, networking, money or credits.

examples.label: Open-source support
examples.text: Generic donation pages, ordinary sponsorship or membership platforms, discounts, trials and paid services without a dedicated open-source program; offers for another project type, license or region; incidental open-source links; applicant-paid access. Grants and bounties that pay you are fine.

examples.label: Credits and resources
examples.text: Public free tiers, ordinary trials, untargeted discounts, sales pages; exhausted capacity; resources only for another project type, license, region or entity. A required card, small co-payment or overage is not paid-only: record it, and exclude only if the benefit is small or {{CONSTRAINTS}} rules it out.

examples.label: Market access
examples.text: Passive directories, startup databases, networking, sales pages, affiliate schemes, paid lead lists, pay-to-play listings, sponsorship packages, registrations without real discovery or buyer access; innovation pages without a defined pilot, customer or procurement path; organizations guessed as customers; pure exposure. A customer-paid pilot is fine.

examples.label: Partnerships
examples.text: Generic "become a partner" pages, sales contacts, contact forms and cold outreach without a partner intake; items where partnership is not the main benefit or the terms are undefined; unverified intermediaries. Record fees, technical work, legal commitments, exclusivity or travel and rank against {{CONSTRAINTS}}.

examples.label: Visibility
examples.text: Conferences, speaker calls, meetups and attend-only routes (EV1, EV2); investor pitches and fundraising contests unless {{CONSTRAINTS}} says you are raising; paid awards, pay-to-play rankings, paid placements, sponsorship packages; directories or contact forms without a selection route; hackathons that need an unrelated build or have no public outcome.

examples.label: Platform programs
examples.text: Integration, affiliate or reseller schemes that do not explain selection and benefit; value limited to a badge, logo or community access; planned capabilities or customers presented as current. A requirement you cannot meet yet (live product, integration, sponsor) makes a candidate conditional at most.

examples.label: Legal, IP and standards
examples.text: Inactive groups, fee-only memberships, opaque legal commitments; pages with no defined route or outcome; invitation- or sponsor-only routes; items whose main benefit is funding, credits or publicity; ordinary paid legal services, templates, unsupported protection or compliance claims. Broad IP assignment, patent pledges, exclusivity or project control make a route conditional at most.

examples.label: Product-only marketing
examples.text: Marketing about the company rather than the product, a founder's personal brand, or an edition that does not exist yet; fundraising and pitch events (PO, FU). A channel that also hosts these still qualifies when {{STARTUP_NAME}} can take part as a product.

examples.label: Investors
examples.text: Inactive investors or those outside your stage, {{SECTOR}} or {{COUNTRY}}; pay-to-pitch events, paid investor lists, intermediaries that charge founders up front.

examples.label: Lenders and platforms
examples.text: Unpublished pricing or terms; providers not licensed or registered where {{COUNTRY}} requires it; advance-fee offers; guarantees or collateral that {{CONSTRAINTS}} rules out.

examples.label: Review run
examples.text: Deleting targets (set a status instead), rewriting someone else's notes, changing a status because a date passed without checking the page, unrelated new targets.

examples.label: Deadline-driven applications
examples.text: Date the next concrete step, not the deadline, after checking eligibility and route. Fixed deadline: start the review 21 days before (30 if a deck, demo, proposal or interview is needed; 14 for a short form), submit 2 to 3 working days early, and note the exact deadline and time zone. With less time, use the next workday only if finishing is realistic, else note the blocker. Rolling route: check and apply within five business days; note the next cohort or capacity limit. Confirm required partners and open blockers first.

examples.label: Conference speaker calls
examples.text: Date each target 2 to 3 weeks before the verified call-for-papers deadline, not the event; add the deadline and event dates as extra dates.

examples.label: Online demo slots
examples.text: Date preparation 1 to 2 days before the event, using the verified slot time in {{TIMEZONE}}; add the event date as an extra date.

examples.label: Community posts
examples.text: Real participation first. Promotional posts at least two days apart, never two on one day, and on the community's promotion day if its rules name one.

examples.label: Launches and submissions
examples.text: Fixed launch date: prepare one working day before and launch on the day. Rolling routes: the next available workday. Never two public launches or two heavy submissions on one day.

examples.label: Credits and provider programs
examples.text: Eligibility and route first, then the application, activation or account setup, early enough to beat capacity limits or windows. Note deadlines, activation windows and credit expiry as separate dates. One resource or platform application per day.

examples.label: Outreach and partner requests
examples.text: Date the earliest open action, not research or the hoped-for result. Once the route is confirmed: preparation, then the application, inquiry or outreach (earlier if integration, security or legal material is needed). Customer, partner and listing actions on separate days. One follow-up 7 to 10 business days after no reply. No speculative outreach.

examples.label: Visibility routes
examples.text: Date the next step, not the ceremony, publication or an expected reply. Rolling route: confirm route and fit, then submit on the next feasible workday. Follow up only when an official response time is published.

examples.label: Legal and governance review
examples.text: Review the applicant, route, signing authority and legal terms before any membership, contribution or application. If ownership, authority or a needed company change is unresolved, schedule that review instead.

examples.label: Campaigns
examples.text: Platform and rules check first, then campaign preparation (page, video, rewards or terms, first supporters) several weeks before launch. Use only dates the platform confirms.

examples.label: Review run
examples.text: Move a date only when the page or the next step changed. Overdue open targets get the next feasible workday, within {{MAX_TARGETS_PER_DAY}}.
